walkthroughs.body_html:
Measurement & Analysis — a core area of Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Measurement & Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Measurement & Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Typical O-H stretch in IR appears at:

options: Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Metal atoms themselves move to carry the current.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice of positive ions, carrying charge.
A dynamic equilibrium means the system is still changing visibly.

mcqs.q: How is a dynamic equilibrium different from a static one?
options: In a dynamic equilibrium, forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates; in a static equilibrium, nothing is happening at the particle level.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Dynamic and static equilibria are the same thing because both show constant macroscopic properties.
A dynamic equilibrium means the system is still changing visibly.

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
